1. ---
2. name: markout
3. description: >-
4.   Source-generated .NET serializer that renders objects as Markdown (also ANSI terminal,
5.   plain text, pretty tables, TSV). Reach for it when a CLI or tool needs structured, human-
6.   or agent-readable output instead of hand-built strings. It looks like System.Text.Json
7.   source generation but the rules differ — there is NO reflection fallback, so it requires a
8.   generated MarkoutSerializerContext and Markout-specific attributes. See the body for the
9.   required pattern.
10. ---
11. 
12. # Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects
13. 
14. Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
15. source generator; no extra package needed).
16. 
17. ## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)
18. 
19. ```csharp
20. using Markout;
21. 
22. // 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
23. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
24. public class Report
25. {
26.     public string Title { get; set; } = "";
27.     public int Count { get; set; }
28.     [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
29.     public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
30. }
31. 
32. [MarkoutSerializable]
33. public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }
34. 
35. // 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
36. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
37. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
38. public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }
39. 
40. // 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
41. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
42. ```
43. 
44. ## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)
45. 
46. - **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
47.   overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
48.   not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
49. - **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
50.   `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
51. - **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
52.   `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
53.   `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
54. - **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
55.   a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
56. - **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
57.   `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.
58. 
59. ## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)
60. 
61. `Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
62. (hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.
63. 
64. ## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)
65. 
66. Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
67. `UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
68. e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`
69.

1. # Markout 2. 3. **Markup adds instructions to content. Markout removes structure from data.** 4. 5. Markout is a source-generated .NET serializer that projects objects into structured, human-readable documents. You annotate your models with attributes that describe data relationships — identity, enumeration, tabulation, measurement, hierarchy — and the source generator emits code that writes through an abstract renderer. The same object graph produces Markdown tables, ANSI terminal output with colored bars, plain text with aligned columns, pretty tables, or TSV rows, without the developer making visual decisions. 6. 7. ## Quick Start 8. 9. ```csharp 10. using Markout; 11. 12. var artist = new Artist( 13. Name: "Sarah McLachlan", 14. Genre: "Pop / Adult Contemporary", 15. Origin: "Halifax, Nova Scotia", 16. DebutYear: 1988, 17. BestKnownFor: "Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia"); 18. 19. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(artist, Console.Out, ArtistContext.Default); 20. 21. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name))] 22. public record Artist( 23. string Name, 24. string Genre, 25. string Origin, 26. int DebutYear, 27. string BestKnownFor); 28. 29. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Artist))] 30. public partial class ArtistContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { } 31. ``` 32. 33. **Output:** 34. 35. ```markdown 36. # Sarah McLachlan 37. 38. | Field | Value | 39. | ----- | ----- | 40. | Genre | Pop / Adult Contemporary | 41. | Origin | Halifax, Nova Scotia | 42. | Debut Year | 1988 | 43. | Best Known For | Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia | 44. ``` 45. 46. Three things: a record, a context, one line of serialization. The `TitleProperty` becomes a heading; everything else renders as a field table. 47. 48. ## Field Layouts 49. 50. The same model renders differently with `FieldLayout`. The default is a two-column table. Switch to `Inline` for a compact summary line: 51. 52. ```csharp 53. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name), FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Inline)] 54. public record Artist( ... ); 55. ``` 56. 57. ```markdown 58. # Sarah McLachlan 59. 60. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary | Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia | Debut Year: 1988 | Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 61. ``` 62. 63. Or `Bulleted` for a list: 64. 65. ```csharp 66. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name), FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Bulleted)] 67. public record Artist( ... ); 68. ``` 69. 70. ```markdown 71. # Sarah McLachlan 72. 73. - Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 74. - Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 75. - Debut Year: 1988 76. - Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 77. ``` 78. 79. Or `Numbered`: 80. 81. ```markdown 82. # Sarah McLachlan 83. 84. 1. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 85. 2. Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 86. 3. Debut Year: 1988 87. 4. Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 88. ``` 89. 90. Or `Plain` — bare lines, no markers. Each line ends with two trailing spaces, which is the markdown signal for `
`: 91. 92. ```markdown 93. # Sarah McLachlan 94. 95. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 96. Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 97. Debut Year: 1988 98. Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 99. ``` 100. 101. The data model doesn't change — only the attribute controls the shape. 102. 103. ## Adding Sections and Tables 104. 105. Add `[MarkoutSection]` to group properties with headings, and use `List` for tables: 106. 107. ```csharp 108. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))] 109. public class CityReport 110. { 111. public string Title { get; set; } = ""; 112. public string Province { get; set; } = ""; 113. public int Population { get; set; } 114. 115. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Landmarks")] 116. public List? Landmarks { get; set; } 117. } 118. 119. [MarkoutSerializable] 120. public class LandmarkRow 121. { 122. public string Name { get; set; } = ""; 123. public string Type { get; set; } = ""; 124. public int Year { get; set; } 125. } 126. 127. [MarkoutContext(typeof(CityReport))] 128. [MarkoutContext(typeof(LandmarkRow))] 129. public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { } 130. 131. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(city, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default); 132. ``` 133. 134. **Output:** 135. 136. ```markdown 137. # Vancouver 138. 139. | Field | Value | 140. | ----- | ----- | 141. | Province | British Columbia | 142. | Population | 2632000 | 143. 144. ## Landmarks 145. 146. | Name | Type | Year | 147. | ----- | ----- | ----- | 148. | Stanley Park | Park | 1888 | 149. | Gastown | Historic | 1867 | 150. | Science World | Museum | 1989 | 151. ``` 152. 153. ## Real-World Example: GitHub Repository Report 154. 155. The [GitHubRepo](samples/GitHubRepo) sample fetches four GitHub API endpoints in parallel and projects the combined JSON into a single report — fields, bar charts, contributor metrics, and release tables — all from one model: 156. 157. ```csharp 158. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title), DescriptionProperty = nameof(Description))] 159. public class RepoInfo 160. { 161. public string Title { get; set; } = ""; 162. 163. [MarkoutIgnore] 164. public string Description { get; set; } = ""; 165. 166. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] 167. public int Stars { get; set; } 168. 169. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] 170. public int Forks { get; set; } 171. 172. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] 173. public int OpenIssues { get; set; } 174. 175. public string Language { get; set; } = ""; 176. public string License { get; set; } = ""; 177. 178. [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] 179. [MarkoutSkipDefault] 180. public Callout ArchivedWarning { get; set; } 181. 182. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Languages")] 183. [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] 184. public List? Languages { get; set; } 185. 186. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Top Contributors")] 187. [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] 188. public List? TopContributors { get; set; } 189. 190. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Releases")] 191. public List? Releases { get; set; } 192. } 193. ``` 194. 195. Run it: 196. 197. ```bash 198. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs # ANSI terminal (default) 199. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format markdown # Markdown 200. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format table # Compact table 201. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format tsv # Stable TSV rows 202. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format jsonl # Stable JSONL rows 203. ``` 204. 205. **Markdown output** for `dotnet/runtime`: 206. 207. ```markdown 208. # dotnet/runtime 209. 210. .NET is a cross-platform runtime for cloud, mobile, desktop, and IoT apps. 211. 212. | Field | Value | 213. | ----- | ----- | 214. | Stars | 17,703 | 215. | Forks | 5,353 | 216. | Open Issues | 8,371 | 217. | Language | C# | 218. | License | MIT License | 219. 220. ## Languages 221. 222. | Category | Count | % | 223. | -------- | ----- | - | 224. | C# | 80 | 83 | 225. | C++ | 9 | 9 | 226. | C | 7 | 7 | 227. 228. ## Top Contributors 229. 230. | Label | Value | 231. | ----- | ----- | 232. | vargaz | 11910 | 233. | stephentoub | 10418 | 234. | kumpera | 4074 | 235. | jkotas | 3245 | 236. 237. ## Releases 238. 239. | Tag | Name | Published | 240. | --- | ---- | --------- | 241. | v8.0.24 | .NET 8.0.24 | 2026-02-10 | 242. | v9.0.13 | v9.0.13 | 2026-02-10 | 243. | v10.0.3 | .NET 10.0.3 | 2026-02-10 | 244. ``` 245. 246. **Table output** — same model, `--format table`: 247. 248. ```text 249. FIELD VALUE 250. Stars 17,703 251. Forks 5,353 252. Open Issues 8,371 253. Language C# 254. License MIT License 255. 256. TAG NAME PUBLISHED 257. v8.0.24 .NET 8.0.24 2026-02-10 258. v9.0.13 v9.0.13 2026-02-10 259. v10.0.3 .NET 10.0.3 2026-02-10 260. ``` 261. 262. **JSONL output** — same table projection, `--format jsonl`: 263. 264. ```jsonl 265. {"tag":"v8.0.24","name":".NET 8.0.24","published":"2026-02-10"} 266. {"tag":"v9.0.13","name":"v9.0.13","published":"2026-02-10"} 267. {"tag":"v10.0.3","name":".NET 10.0.3","published":"2026-02-10"} 268. ``` 269. 270. The pattern is always the same: deserialize your API data, project to a model, serialize. Markout handles the rest. 271. 272. ## Shape Library 273. 274. Each property on a model maps to a data relationship, not a visual element. Renderers decide how to present each shape. 275. 276. | Relationship | C# type | What it means | Markdown | ANSI | 277. |---|---|---|---|---| 278. | **Identity** | `string`, `int`, `bool` | Named value | `Key: value` | Bold key, value | 279. | **Enumeration** | `string[]` | Sequence of items | `- item` | Bullet list | 280. | **Tabulation** | `List` | Uniform records | `\| col \| col \|` | Space-padded table | 281. | **Section** | `[MarkoutSection]` | Logical grouping | `## Heading` | Colored heading | 282. | **Description** | `List` | Terms with explanations | `- **Term:** text` | Bold term, text | 283. | **Measurement** | `List` | Comparative quantities | `Label ████░░ 45` | Colored bars | 284. | **Composition** | `List` | Parts of a whole | `██▓▓▒░` stacked | Colored segments | 285. | **Hierarchy** | `List` | Parent-child structure | `├── node` | Box-drawing tree | 286. | **Quotation** | `CodeSection` | Verbatim content | ` ```code``` ` | Syntax display | 287. | **Attention** | `Callout` | Important messages | `> [!WARNING]` | Colored label | 288. 289. Plus structural shapes: **Quotation** (prose quotation), **Matrix** (2D pivot grid), **Rule** (section separator). 290. 291. ### Record Types 292. 293. Shapes that need structured input provide record types named for what the data *is*, not what it *looks like*: 294. 295. ```csharp 296. new Metric("Build Time", 4.2) // measurement 297. new Description("dotnet-inspect", "API surface inspection tool") // term + explanation 298. new Breakdown("Jan 2025", [new("Critical", 1), new("High", 3)]) // proportional composition 299. new Callout(CalloutSeverity.Warning, "3 vulnerabilities found") // attention 300. new CodeSection("csharp", "public class Foo { }") // verbatim content 301. ``` 302. 303. ## Renderers 304. 305. Markout ships five formatters. The serializer writes through `MarkoutWriter` (the orchestrator) — swap the formatter, change the output. 306. 307. | Formatter | Output | Use case | 308. |---|---|---| 309. | **MarkdownFormatter** | GitHub-Flavored Markdown | Documentation, LLM tool output, rendered reports | 310. | **PlainTextFormatter** | Plain text without markup | Minimal output, no syntax characters | 311. | **UnicodeFormatter** | Box-drawing characters | Rich tables with borders, no color | 312. | **TableFormatter** | Tables, lists, fields | Compact summaries, pretty tables, TSV/JSONL rows | 313. | **DiagramFormatter** | Trees and structural diagrams | Dependency graphs, file trees | 314. 315. Optional packages: 316. 317. | Package | Formatter | Use case | 318. |---|---|---| 319. | **Markout.Ansi.Spectre** | `SpectreFormatter` | Rich terminal UI via Spectre.Console | 320. 321. Formatters declare which shapes they support by implementing capability interfaces (`ITableFormatter`, `IFieldFormatter`, `ITreeFormatter`, etc.). Unsupported shapes are silently skipped — the data is never lost, only the visual sophistication changes. 322. 323. ### Format promises 324. 325. - Markdown table-cell and heading text is treated as literal data: the structural characters `&`, `<`, `>`, and backtick are escaped to entities (`&`, `<`, `>`, ```) so the value renders verbatim rather than being interpreted as HTML or a code span. Table cells additionally normalize the delimiting pipe to `|`. 326. - The exception is content inside a rendered `` span, where those characters are literal: there, a pipe is escaped as `\|` (GFM unescapes it while splitting table rows, before code-span parsing) and angle brackets/ampersands need no escaping. 327. - Semantic inline `...` tags render as Markdown code spans and as plain text in table, TSV, and JSONL output. 328. - `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Tsv` uses stable snake_case headers by default and never emits embedded tabs or newlines in table cells. 329. - `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Jsonl` uses stable snake_case property names by default and emits one JSON object per table row. 330. - `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Pretty` renders the same projection as TSV, with each column starting at a uniform position across rows. 331. 332. ## Templates 333. 334. Templates let you author document structure in Markdown and fill data slots at runtime. The same template renders to any format — Markdown, plain text, or ANSI terminal. 335. 336. **template.md:** 337. 338. ```markdown 339. # .NET Security Report for {{date}} 340. 341. The following vulnerabilities were disclosed this month. 342. 343. {{vuln-table}} 344. 345. | Level | CVSS Range | Response | 346. | ----- | ---------- | -------- | 347. | Critical | 9.0–10.0 | Patch immediately | 348. | High | 7.0–8.9 | Patch within 30 days | 349. 350. {{#if commits}} 351. ## Commits 352. 353. {{commit-table}} 354. {{/if}} 355. ``` 356. 357. **Program.cs:** 358. 359. ```csharp 360. using Markout; 361. using Markout.Templates; 362. 363. var template = MarkoutTemplate.Load("template.md"); 364. template.TableOptions = new TableFormatterOptions(); // smooth column widths 365. 366. template.Bind("date", "February 2026"); 367. template.Bind("vuln-table", vulnerabilityData); // IMarkoutFormattable 368. template.Bind("commits", hasCommits ? "yes" : null); 369. template.Bind("commit-table", commitData); 370. 371. // Markdown output 372. Console.WriteLine(template.Render(new MarkoutWriterOptions { PrettyTables = true })); 373. 374. // Plain text output — same template, different formatter 375. var plainWriter = new MarkoutWriter(Console.Out, new UnicodeFormatter()); 376. template.Render(plainWriter); 377. ``` 378. 379. Templates support: 380. 381. - **`{{key}}`** — inline substitution in headings and prose, or block-level data rendering 382. - **`{{#if key}}`** / **`{{/if}}`** — conditional sections (included when key is bound and non-null) 383. - **Pipe tables** — parsed and re-rendered through the writer's table shape, with optional statistical column-width optimization 384. - **`IMarkoutFormattable`** and **`MarkoutTypeInfo`** bindings for shape-aware data rendering 385. 386. ```bash 387. dotnet add package Markout.Templates 388. ``` 389. 390. ### Template Runner Tool 391. 392. A basic CLI tool is included for rendering templates with string bindings: 393. 394. ```bash 395. dotnet run --project tools/markout-template -- template.md date="February 2026" title="Report" 396. ``` 397. 398. Unbound block placeholders are skipped, so you can render partial templates. Pipe `key=value` lines on stdin for additional bindings. 399. 400. ## Customization Layers 401. 402. Markout provides multiple layers of control, from zero-config to full custom: 403. 404. **Layer 1 — Attributes** (compile-time): Control what's rendered and how. 405. 406. ```csharp 407. [MarkoutPropertyName("Born")] // rename a field 408. [MarkoutSkipNull] // hide when null 409. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Details")] // group into a section 410. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("N0")] // format numbers 411. [MarkoutShowWhen(nameof(HasDetails))] // conditional rendering 412. [MarkoutMaxItems(10)] // truncate long lists 413. [MarkoutSection(FieldOrder = MarkoutFieldOrder.Alphabetical)] // alpha-order field rows 414. [MarkoutValueMap("k=badge", ...)] // map values to badge-prefixed output 415. [MarkoutUnwrap] // inline collection items without section heading 416. [MarkoutIgnoreColumnWhen(...)] // conditionally hide table columns 417. ``` 418. 419. **Layer 2 — Writer Options** (runtime): Control which sections appear. 420. 421. ```csharp 422. var options = new MarkoutWriterOptions 423. { 424. IncludeSections = new HashSet { "Summary", "Errors" }, // only these sections 425. BoldFieldNames = true 426. }; 427. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new MarkdownFormatter(), context, options); 428. ``` 429. 430. **Layer 3 — Custom Formatter** (code): Implement capability interfaces for custom rendering. 431. 432. ```csharp 433. public class MyFormatter : IMarkoutFormatter, IFieldFormatter, ITableFormatter 434. { 435. // Implement only the interfaces your formatter supports 436. void IFieldFormatter.FormatFieldName(TextWriter w, string key, bool bold) { ... } 437. void ITableFormatter.FormatTable(TextWriter w, ReadOnlySpan headers, IList rows, int skippedRows, MarkoutWriterOptions options) { ... } 438. } 439. ``` 440. 441. ## Installation 442. 443. ```bash 444. dotnet add package Markout 445. ``` 446. 447. The package includes the source generator — no additional packages needed. 448. 449. ## Samples 450. 451. - **[HelloMarkout](samples/HelloMarkout)** — Simplest possible example: a class, a context, one line of serialization 452. - **[RecordDemo](samples/RecordDemo)** — Records as data models 453. - **[GitHubRepo](samples/GitHubRepo)** — GitHub API → fields, breakdowns, metrics, and tables with Spectre, Markdown, table, TSV, and JSONL output 454. - **[GitHubActivity](samples/GitHubActivity)** — User profile and recent events from the GitHub API 455. - **[CanadianContent](samples/CanadianContent)** — Canadian actors and shows with tables, trees, metrics, and multiple renderers 456. - **[LatestCves](samples/LatestCves)** — .NET security advisories with trees and severity breakdowns 457. - **[DotNetReleases](samples/DotNetReleases)** — .NET release information from GitHub 458. - **[Serialization](samples/Serialization)** — Shape gallery, section filtering, and writer API examples 459. - **[TemplateDemo](samples/TemplateDemo)** — Document template with inline tables, conditional sections, and multi-format rendering 460. 461. ## Formats and Agents 462. 463. Agents and LLMs are skilled at two things: using tools and reading text. No single text format is best in all cases — a tool that can produce results in multiple formats is more useful to an agent than one locked to a single output. 464. 465. JSON and Markout are peer options. JSON carries data between systems — APIs, config, round-trip serialization. Markout carries data to readers — humans and agents consuming structured documents. A tool like [dotnet-inspect](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect) gathers data from NuGet packages, assemblies, and APIs, projects it into Markout models, and offers both `--json` and Markout output. The same section metadata, schema discovery, and projection features enable control and customization upstream of either format generation. 466. 467. Tools that produce a lot of text need standard controls to segment it. Verbosity levels are useful but blunt — they control *how much* without letting you say *which parts*. Markout's section selection (`-s Dependencies`) and column/field projection (`--columns Name,Version`) are sharper instruments, offering the kind of targeted trimming that [Go templates](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) provide in other ecosystems, but without requiring users to learn a template language. You say what data to keep; the renderer decides how to present it. 468. 469. Tools built on a shared output scheme improve together. When eval sessions reveal that a heading level, table layout, or field ordering works better for agents, a new Markout version carries that improvement to every tool that uses it. 470. 471. ## For Coding Agents 472. 473. If you are an LLM or coding agent building a CLI tool that needs structured, readable output, see **[SKILL.md](SKILL.md)** for step-by-step integration instructions and attribute reference. 474. 475. ## Real-World Usage 476. 477. # Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects

Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
source generator; no extra package needed).

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

```csharp
using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
    public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
}

[MarkoutSerializable]
public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }

// 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }

// 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
```

## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
  overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
  not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
  `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
  `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
  `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

`Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
(hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.

## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)

Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
`UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`

# Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects

source generator; no extra package needed).

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

```csharp
using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
    public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
}

[MarkoutSerializable]
public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }

// 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }

// 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
```

## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
  overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
  not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
  `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
  `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
  `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

`Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
(hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.

## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)

Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
`UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).

Contents of https://www.nuget.org/packages/Markout/0.13.8: **Markup adds instructions to content. Markout removes structure from data.** Markout is a source-generated .NET serializer that projects objects into structured, human-readable documents. You annotate your models with attributes that describe data relationships — identity, enumeration, tabulation, measurement, hierarchy — and the source generator emits code that writes through an abstract renderer. The same object graph produces Markdown tables, ANSI terminal output with colored bars, plain text with aligned columns, pretty tables, or TSV rows, without the developer making visual decisions. ### Quick Start ``` using Markout; var artist = new Artist( Name: "Sarah McLachlan", Genre: "Pop / Adult Contemporary", Origin: "Halifax, Nova Scotia", DebutYear: 1988, BestKnownFor: "Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia"); MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(artist, Console.Out, ArtistContext.Default); [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name))] public record Artist( string Name, string Genre, string Origin, int DebutYear, string BestKnownFor); [MarkoutContext(typeof(Artist))] public partial class ArtistContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { } ``` **Output:** ``` # Sarah McLachlan | Field | Value | | ----- | ----- | | Genre | Pop / Adult Contemporary | | Origin | Halifax, Nova Scotia | | Debut Year | 1988 | | Best Known For | Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia | ``` Three things: a record, a context, one line of serialization. The `TitleProperty` becomes a heading; everything else renders as a field table. ### Field Layouts The same model renders differently with `FieldLayout`. The default is a two-column table. Switch to `Inline` for a compact summary line: ``` [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name), FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Inline)] public record Artist( ... ); ``` ``` # Sarah McLachlan Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary | Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia | Debut Year: 1988 | Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia ``` Or `Bulleted` for a list: ``` [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name), FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Bulleted)] public record Artist( ... ); ``` ``` # Sarah McLachlan - Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary - Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia - Debut Year: 1988 - Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia ``` Or `Numbered`: ``` # Sarah McLachlan 1. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 2. Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 3. Debut Year: 1988 4. Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia ``` Or `Plain` — bare lines, no markers. Each line ends with two trailing spaces, which is the markdown signal for `
`: ``` # Sarah McLachlan Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia Debut Year: 1988 Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia ``` The data model doesn't change — only the attribute controls the shape. ### Adding Sections and Tables Add `[MarkoutSection]` to group properties with headings, and use `List` for tables: ``` [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))] public class CityReport { public string Title { get; set; } = ""; public string Province { get; set; } = ""; public int Population { get; set; } [MarkoutSection(Name = "Landmarks")] public List? Landmarks { get; set; } } [MarkoutSerializable] public class LandmarkRow { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Type { get; set; } = ""; public int Year { get; set; } } [MarkoutContext(typeof(CityReport))] [MarkoutContext(typeof(LandmarkRow))] public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { } MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(city, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default); ``` **Output:** ``` # Vancouver | Field | Value | | ----- | ----- | | Province | British Columbia | | Population | 2632000 | ## Landmarks | Name | Type | Year | | ----- | ----- | ----- | | Stanley Park | Park | 1888 | | Gastown | Historic | 1867 | | Science World | Museum | 1989 | ``` ### Real-World Example: GitHub Repository Report The GitHubRepo sample fetches four GitHub API endpoints in parallel and projects the combined JSON into a single report — fields, bar charts, contributor metrics, and release tables — all from one model: ``` [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title), DescriptionProperty = nameof(Description))] public class RepoInfo { public string Title { get; set; } = ""; [MarkoutIgnore] public string Description { get; set; } = ""; [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] public int Stars { get; set; } [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] public int Forks { get; set; } [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] public int OpenIssues { get; set; } public string Language { get; set; } = ""; public string License { get; set; } = ""; [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] [MarkoutSkipDefault] public Callout ArchivedWarning { get; set; } [MarkoutSection(Name = "Languages")] [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] public List? #### Record Types

Shapes that need structured input provide record types named for what the data _is_, not what it _looks like_:

Table cells additionally normalize the delimiting pipe to `|`. * The exception is content inside a rendered `` span, where those characters are literal: there, a pipe is escaped as `\|` (GFM unescapes it while splitting table rows, before code-span parsing) and angle brackets/ampersands need no escaping. * Semantic inline `...` tags render as Markdown code spans and as plain text in table, TSV, and JSONL output. * `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Tsv` uses stable snake\_case headers by default and never emits embedded tabs or newlines in table cells. * `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Jsonl` uses stable snake\_case property names by default and emits one JSON object per table row. * `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Pretty` renders the same projection as TSV, with each column starting at a uniform position across rows. ### Templates Templates let you author document structure in Markdown and fill data slots at runtime. The same template renders to any format — Markdown, plain text, or ANSI terminal. **template.md:** ``` # .NET Security Report for {{date}} The following vulnerabilities were disclosed this month. {{vuln-table}} | Level | CVSS Range | Response | | ----- | ---------- | -------- | | Critical | 9.0–10.0 | Patch immediately | | High | 7.0–8.9 | Patch within 30 days | {{#if commits}} ## Commits {{commit-table}} {{/if}} ``` **Program.cs:** ``` using Markout; using Markout.Templates; var template = MarkoutTemplate.Load("template.md"); template.TableOptions = new TableFormatterOptions(); // smooth column widths template.Bind("date", "February 2026"); template.Bind("vuln-table", vulnerabilityData); // IMarkoutFormattable template.Bind("commits", hasCommits ? "yes" : null); template.Bind("commit-table", commitData); // Markdown output Console.WriteLine(template.Render(new MarkoutWriterOptions { PrettyTables = true })); // Plain text output — same template, different formatter var plainWriter = new MarkoutWriter(Console.Out, new UnicodeFormatter()); template.Render(plainWriter); ``` Templates support: * **`{{key}}`** — inline substitution in headings and prose, or block-level data rendering * **`{{#if key}}`** / **`{{/if}}`** — conditional sections (included when key is bound and non-null) * **Pipe tables** — parsed and re-rendered through the writer's table shape, with optional statistical column-width optimization * **`IMarkoutFormattable`** and **`MarkoutTypeInfo`** bindings for shape-aware data rendering ``` dotnet add package Markout.Templates ``` #### Template Runner Tool A basic CLI tool is included for rendering templates with string bindings: ``` dotnet run --project tools/markout-template -- template.md date="February 2026" title="Report" ``` Unbound block placeholders are skipped, so you can render partial templates. Pipe `key=value` lines on stdin for additional bindings. ### Customization Layers Markout provides multiple layers of control, from zero-config to full custom: **Layer 1 — Attributes** (compile-time): Control what's rendered and how. ``` [MarkoutPropertyName("Born")] // rename a field [MarkoutSkipNull] // hide when null [MarkoutSection(Name = "Details")] // group into a section [MarkoutDisplayFormat("N0")] // format numbers [MarkoutShowWhen(nameof(HasDetails))] // conditional rendering [MarkoutMaxItems(10)] // truncate long lists [MarkoutSection(FieldOrder = MarkoutFieldOrder.Alphabetical)] // alpha-order field rows [MarkoutValueMap("k=badge", ...)] // map values to badge-prefixed output [MarkoutUnwrap] // inline collection items without section heading [MarkoutIgnoreColumnWhen(...)] // conditionally hide table columns ``` **Layer 2 — Writer Options** (runtime): Control which sections appear. ``` var options = new MarkoutWriterOptions { IncludeSections = new HashSet { "Summary", "Errors" }, // only these sections BoldFieldNames = true }; MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new MarkdownFormatter(), context, options); ``` **Layer 3 — Custom Formatter** (code): Implement capability interfaces for custom rendering. ``` public class MyFormatter : IMarkoutFormatter, IFieldFormatter, ITableFormatter { // Implement only the interfaces your formatter supports void IFieldFormatter.FormatFieldName(TextWriter w, string key, bool bold) { ... } void ITableFormatter.FormatTable(TextWriter w, ReadOnlySpan headers, IList rows, int skippedRows, MarkoutWriterOptions options) { ... } } ``` ### Installation ``` dotnet add package Markout ``` The package includes the source generator — no additional packages needed. ### Samples * **HelloMarkout** — Simplest possib Content truncated. # Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects

Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
source generator; no extra package needed).

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

```csharp
using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
    public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
}

[MarkoutSerializable]
public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }

// 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }

// 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
```

## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
  overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
  not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
  `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
  `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
  `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

`Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
(hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.

## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)

Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
`UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`

# Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects

Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
source generator; no extra package needed).

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

```csharp
using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
    public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
}

[MarkoutSerializable]
public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }

// 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }

// 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
```

## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
  overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
  not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
  `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
  `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
  `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,

1. # Markout 2. 3. **Markup adds instructions to content. Markout removes structure from data.** 4. 5. Markout is a source-generated .NET serializer that projects objects into structured, human-readable documents. You annotate your models with attributes that describe data relationships — identity, enumeration, tabulation, measurement, hierarchy — and the source generator emits code that writes through an abstract renderer. The same object graph produces Markdown tables, ANSI terminal output with colored bars, plain text with aligned columns, pretty tables, or TSV rows, without the developer making visual decisions. 6. 7. ## Quick Start 8. 9. ```csharp 10. using Markout; 11. 12. var artist = new Artist( 13. Name: "Sarah McLachlan", 14. Genre: "Pop / Adult Contemporary", 15. Origin: "Halifax, Nova Scotia", 16. DebutYear: 1988, 17. BestKnownFor: "Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia"); 18. 19. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(artist, Console.Out, ArtistContext.Default); 20. 21. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name))] 22. public record Artist( 23. string Name, 24. string Genre, 25. string Origin, 26. int DebutYear, 27. string BestKnownFor); 28. 29. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Artist))] 30. public partial class ArtistContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { } 31. ``` 32. 33. **Output:** 34. 35. ```markdown 36. # Sarah McLachlan 37. 38. | Field | Value | 39. | ----- | ----- | 40. | Genre | Pop / Adult Contemporary | 41. | Origin | Halifax, Nova Scotia | 42. | Debut Year | 1988 | 43. | Best Known For | Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia | 44. ``` 45. 46. Three things: a record, a context, one line of serialization. The `TitleProperty` becomes a heading; everything else renders as a field table. 47. 48. ## Field Layouts 49. 50. The same model renders differently with `FieldLayout`. The default is a two-column table. Switch to `Inline` for a compact summary line: 51. 52. ```csharp 53. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name), FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Inline)] 54. public record Artist( ... ); 55. ``` 56. 57. ```markdown 58. # Sarah McLachlan 59. 60. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary | Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia | Debut Year: 1988 | Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 61. ``` 62. 63. Or `Bulleted` for a list: 64. 65. ```csharp 66. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Artist.Name), FieldLayout = FieldLayout.Bulleted)] 67. public record Artist( ... ); 68. ``` 69. 70. ```markdown 71. # Sarah McLachlan 72. 73. - Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 74. - Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 75. - Debut Year: 1988 76. - Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 77. ``` 78. 79. Or `Numbered`: 80. 81. ```markdown 82. # Sarah McLachlan 83. 84. 1. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 85. 2. Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 86. 3. Debut Year: 1988 87. 4. Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 88. ``` 89. 90. Or `Plain` — bare lines, no markers. Each line ends with two trailing spaces, which is the markdown signal for `
`: 91. 92. ```markdown 93. # Sarah McLachlan 94. 95. Genre: Pop / Adult Contemporary 96. Origin: Halifax, Nova Scotia 97. Debut Year: 1988 98. Best Known For: Angel, Building a Mystery, Adia 99. ``` 100. 101. The data model doesn't change — only the attribute controls the shape. 102. 103. ## Adding Sections and Tables 104. 105. Add `[MarkoutSection]` to group properties with headings, and use `List` for tables: 106. 107. ```csharp 108. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))] 109. public class CityReport 110. { 111. public string Title { get; set; } = ""; 112. public string Province { get; set; } = ""; 113. public int Population { get; set; } 114. 115. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Landmarks")] 116. public List? Landmarks { get; set; } 117. } 118. 119. [MarkoutSerializable] 120. public class LandmarkRow 121. { 122. public string Name { get; set; } = ""; 123. public string Type { get; set; } = ""; 124. public int Year { get; set; } 125. } 126. 127. [MarkoutContext(typeof(CityReport))] 128. [MarkoutContext(typeof(LandmarkRow))] 129. public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { } 130. 131. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(city, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default); 132. ``` 133. 134. **Output:** 135. 136. ```markdown 137. # Vancouver 138. 139. | Field | Value | 140. | ----- | ----- | 141. | Province | British Columbia | 142. | Population | 2632000 | 143. 144. ## Landmarks 145. 146. | Name | Type | Year | 147. | ----- | ----- | ----- | 148. | Stanley Park | Park | 1888 | 149. | Gastown | Historic | 1867 | 150. | Science World | Museum | 1989 | 151. ``` 152. 153. ## Real-World Example: GitHub Repository Report 154. 155. The [GitHubRepo](samples/GitHubRepo) sample fetches four GitHub API endpoints in parallel and projects the combined JSON into a single report — fields, bar charts, contributor metrics, and release tables — all from one model: 156. 157. ```csharp 158. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title), DescriptionProperty = nameof(Description))] 159. public class RepoInfo 160. { 161. public string Title { get; set; } = ""; 162. 163. [MarkoutIgnore] 164. public string Description { get; set; } = ""; 165. 166. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] 167. public int Stars { get; set; } 168. 169. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] 170. public int Forks { get; set; } 171. 172. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("{0:N0}")] 173. public int OpenIssues { get; set; } 174. 175. public string Language { get; set; } = ""; 176. public string License { get; set; } = ""; 177. 178. [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] 179. [MarkoutSkipDefault] 180. public Callout ArchivedWarning { get; set; } 181. 182. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Languages")] 183. [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] 184. public List? Languages { get; set; } 185. 186. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Top Contributors")] 187. [MarkoutIgnoreInTable] 188. public List? TopContributors { get; set; } 189. 190. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Releases")] 191. public List? Releases { get; set; } 192. } 193. ``` 194. 195. Run it: 196. 197. ```bash 198. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs # ANSI terminal (default) 199. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format markdown # Markdown 200. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format table # Compact table 201. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format tsv # Stable TSV rows 202. dotnet run samples/GitHubRepo/GitHubRepo.cs -- dotnet/runtime --format jsonl # Stable JSONL rows 203. ``` 204. 205. **Markdown output** for `dotnet/runtime`: 206. 207. ```markdown 208. # dotnet/runtime 209. 210. .NET is a cross-platform runtime for cloud, mobile, desktop, and IoT apps. 211. 212. | Field | Value | 213. | ----- | ----- | 214. | Stars | 17,703 | 215. | Forks | 5,353 | 216. | Open Issues | 8,371 | 217. | Language | C# | 218. | License | MIT License | 219. 220. ## Languages 221. 222. | Category | Count | % | 223. | -------- | ----- | - | 224. | C# | 80 | 83 | 225. | C++ | 9 | 9 | 226. | C | 7 | 7 | 227. 228. ## Top Contributors 229. 230. | Label | Value | 231. | ----- | ----- | 232. | vargaz | 11910 | 233. | stephentoub | 10418 | 234. | kumpera | 4074 | 235. | jkotas | 3245 | 236. 237. ## Releases 238. 239. | Tag | Name | Published | 240. | --- | ---- | --------- | 241. | v8.0.24 | .NET 8.0.24 | 2026-02-10 | 242. | v9.0.13 | v9.0.13 | 2026-02-10 | 243. | v10.0.3 | .NET 10.0.3 | 2026-02-10 | 244. ``` 245. 246. **Table output** — same model, `--format table`: 247. 248. ```text 249. FIELD VALUE 250. Stars 17,703 251. Forks 5,353 252. Open Issues 8,371 253. Language C# 254. License MIT License 255. 256. TAG NAME PUBLISHED 257. v8.0.24 .NET 8.0.24 2026-02-10 258. v9.0.13 v9.0.13 2026-02-10 259. v10.0.3 .NET 10.0.3 2026-02-10 260. ``` 261. 262. **JSONL output** — same table projection, `--format jsonl`: 263. 264. ```jsonl 265. {"tag":"v8.0.24","name":".NET 8.0.24","published":"2026-02-10"} 266. {"tag":"v9.0.13","name":"v9.0.13","published":"2026-02-10"} 267. {"tag":"v10.0.3","name":".NET 10.0.3","published":"2026-02-10"} 268. ``` 269. 270. The pattern is always the same: deserialize your API data, project to a model, serialize. Markout handles the rest. 271. 272. ## Shape Library 273. 274. Each property on a model maps to a data relationship, not a visual element. Renderers decide how to present each shape. 275. 276. | Relationship | C# type | What it means | Markdown | ANSI | 277. |---|---|---|---|---| 278. | **Identity** | `string`, `int`, `bool` | Named value | `Key: value` | Bold key, value | 279. | **Enumeration** | `string[]` | Sequence of items | `- item` | Bullet list | 280. | **Tabulation** | `List` | Uniform records | `\| col \| col \|` | Space-padded table | 281. | **Section** | `[MarkoutSection]` | Logical grouping | `## Heading` | Colored heading | 282. | **Description** | `List` | Terms with explanations | `- **Term:** text` | Bold term, text | 283. | **Measurement** | `List` | Comparative quantities | `Label ████░░ 45` | Colored bars | 284. | **Composition** | `List` | Parts of a whole | `██▓▓▒░` stacked | Colored segments | 285. | **Hierarchy** | `List` | Parent-child structure | `├── node` | Box-drawing tree | 286. | **Quotation** | `CodeSection` | Verbatim content | ` ```code``` ` | Syntax display | 287. | **Attention** | `Callout` | Important messages | `> [!WARNING]` | Colored label | 288. 289. Plus structural shapes: **Quotation** (prose quotation), **Matrix** (2D pivot grid), **Rule** (section separator). 290. 291. ### Record Types 292. 293. Shapes that need structured input provide record types named for what the data *is*, not what it *looks like*: 294. 295. ```csharp 296. new Metric("Build Time", 4.2) // measurement 297. new Description("dotnet-inspect", "API surface inspection tool") // term + explanation 298. new Breakdown("Jan 2025", [new("Critical", 1), new("High", 3)]) // proportional composition 299. new Callout(CalloutSeverity.Warning, "3 vulnerabilities found") // attention 300. new CodeSection("csharp", "public class Foo { }") // verbatim content 301. ``` 302. 303. ## Renderers 304. 305. Markout ships five formatters. The serializer writes through `MarkoutWriter` (the orchestrator) — swap the formatter, change the output. 306. 307. | Formatter | Output | Use case | 308. |---|---|---| 309. | **MarkdownFormatter** | GitHub-Flavored Markdown | Documentation, LLM tool output, rendered reports | 310. | **PlainTextFormatter** | Plain text without markup | Minimal output, no syntax characters | 311. | **UnicodeFormatter** | Box-drawing characters | Rich tables with borders, no color | 312. | **TableFormatter** | Tables, lists, fields | Compact summaries, pretty tables, TSV/JSONL rows | 313. | **DiagramFormatter** | Trees and structural diagrams | Dependency graphs, file trees | 314. 315. Optional packages: 316. 317. | Package | Formatter | Use case | 318. |---|---|---| 319. | **Markout.Ansi.Spectre** | `SpectreFormatter` | Rich terminal UI via Spectre.Console | 320. 321. Formatters declare which shapes they support by implementing capability interfaces (`ITableFormatter`, `IFieldFormatter`, `ITreeFormatter`, etc.). Unsupported shapes are silently skipped — the data is never lost, only the visual sophistication changes. 322. 323. ### Format promises 324. 325. - Markdown table-cell and heading text is treated as literal data: the structural characters `&`, `<`, `>`, and backtick are escaped to entities (`&`, `<`, `>`, ```) so the value renders verbatim rather than being interpreted as HTML or a code span. Table cells additionally normalize the delimiting pipe to `|`. 326. - The exception is content inside a rendered `` span, where those characters are literal: there, a pipe is escaped as `\|` (GFM unescapes it while splitting table rows, before code-span parsing) and angle brackets/ampersands need no escaping. 327. - Semantic inline `...` tags render as Markdown code spans and as plain text in table, TSV, and JSONL output. 328. - `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Tsv` uses stable snake_case headers by default and never emits embedded tabs or newlines in table cells. 329. - `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Jsonl` uses stable snake_case property names by default and emits one JSON object per table row. 330. - `TableFormatter` with `MarkoutTableMode.Pretty` renders the same projection as TSV, with each column starting at a uniform position across rows. 331. 332. ## Templates 333. 334. Templates let you author document structure in Markdown and fill data slots at runtime. The same template renders to any format — Markdown, plain text, or ANSI terminal. 335. 336. **template.md:** 337. 338. ```markdown 339. # .NET Security Report for {{date}} 340. 341. The following vulnerabilities were disclosed this month. 342. 343. {{vuln-table}} 344. 345. | Level | CVSS Range | Response | 346. | ----- | ---------- | -------- | 347. | Critical | 9.0–10.0 | Patch immediately | 348. | High | 7.0–8.9 | Patch within 30 days | 349. 350. {{#if commits}} 351. ## Commits 352. 353. {{commit-table}} 354. {{/if}} 355. ``` 356. 357. **Program.cs:** 358. 359. ```csharp 360. using Markout; 361. using Markout.Templates; 362. 363. var template = MarkoutTemplate.Load("template.md"); 364. template.TableOptions = new TableFormatterOptions(); // smooth column widths 365. 366. template.Bind("date", "February 2026"); 367. template.Bind("vuln-table", vulnerabilityData); // IMarkoutFormattable 368. template.Bind("commits", hasCommits ? "yes" : null); 369. template.Bind("commit-table", commitData); 370. 371. // Markdown output 372. Console.WriteLine(template.Render(new MarkoutWriterOptions { PrettyTables = true })); 373. 374. // Plain text output — same template, different formatter 375. var plainWriter = new MarkoutWriter(Console.Out, new UnicodeFormatter()); 376. template.Render(plainWriter); 377. ``` 378. 379. Templates support: 380. 381. - **`{{key}}`** — inline substitution in headings and prose, or block-level data rendering 382. - **`{{#if key}}`** / **`{{/if}}`** — conditional sections (included when key is bound and non-null) 383. - **Pipe tables** — parsed and re-rendered through the writer's table shape, with optional statistical column-width optimization 384. - **`IMarkoutFormattable`** and **`MarkoutTypeInfo`** bindings for shape-aware data rendering 385. 386. ```bash 387. dotnet add package Markout.Templates 388. ``` 389. 390. ### Template Runner Tool 391. 392. A basic CLI tool is included for rendering templates with string bindings: 393. 394. ```bash 395. dotnet run --project tools/markout-template -- template.md date="February 2026" title="Report" 396. ``` 397. 398. Unbound block placeholders are skipped, so you can render partial templates. Pipe `key=value` lines on stdin for additional bindings. 399. 400. ## Customization Layers 401. 402. Markout provides multiple layers of control, from zero-config to full custom: 403. 404. **Layer 1 — Attributes** (compile-time): Control what's rendered and how. 405. 406. ```csharp 407. [MarkoutPropertyName("Born")] // rename a field 408. [MarkoutSkipNull] // hide when null 409. [MarkoutSection(Name = "Details")] // group into a section 410. [MarkoutDisplayFormat("N0")] // format numbers 411. [MarkoutShowWhen(nameof(HasDetails))] // conditional rendering 412. [MarkoutMaxItems(10)] // truncate long lists 413. [MarkoutSection(FieldOrder = MarkoutFieldOrder.Alphabetical)] // alpha-order field rows 414. [MarkoutValueMap("k=badge", ...)] // map values to badge-prefixed output 415. [MarkoutUnwrap] // inline collection items without section heading 416. [MarkoutIgnoreColumnWhen(...)] // conditionally hide table columns 417. ``` 418. 419. **Layer 2 — Writer Options** (runtime): Control which sections appear. 420. 421. ```csharp 422. var options = new MarkoutWriterOptions 423. { 424. IncludeSections = new HashSet { "Summary", "Errors" }, // only these sections 425. BoldFieldNames = true 426. }; 427. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(view, Console.Out, new MarkdownFormatter(), context, options); 428. ``` 429. 430. **Layer 3 — Custom Formatter** (code): Implement capability interfaces for custom rendering. 431. 432. ```csharp 433. public class MyFormatter : IMarkoutFormatter, IFieldFormatter, ITableFormatter 434. { 435. // Implement only the interfaces your formatter supports 436. void IFieldFormatter.FormatFieldName(TextWriter w, string key, bool bold) { ... } 437. void ITableFormatter.FormatTable(TextWriter w, ReadOnlySpan headers, IList rows, int skippedRows, MarkoutWriterOptions options) { ... } 438. } 439. ``` 440. 441. ## Installation 442. 443. ```bash 444. dotnet add package Markout 445. ``` 446. 447. The package includes the source generator — no additional packages needed. 448. 449. ## Samples 450. 451. - **[HelloMarkout](samples/HelloMarkout)** — Simplest possible example: a class, a context, one line of serialization 452. - **[RecordDemo](samples/RecordDemo)** — Records as data models 453. - **[GitHubRepo](samples/GitHubRepo)** — GitHub API → fields, breakdowns, metrics, and tables with Spectre, Markdown, table, TSV, and JSONL output 454. - **[GitHubActivity](samples/GitHubActivity)** — User profile and recent events from the GitHub API 455. - **[CanadianContent](samples/CanadianContent)** — Canadian actors and shows with tables, trees, metrics, and multiple renderers 456. - **[LatestCves](samples/LatestCves)** — .NET security advisories with trees and severity breakdowns 457. - **[DotNetReleases](samples/DotNetReleases)** — .NET release information from GitHub 458. - **[Serialization](samples/Serialization)** — Shape gallery, section filtering, and writer API examples 459. - **[TemplateDemo](samples/TemplateDemo)** — Document template with inline tables, conditional sections, and multi-format rendering 460. 461. ## Formats and Agents 462. 463. Agents and LLMs are skilled at two things: using tools and reading text. No single text format is best in all cases — a tool that can produce results in multiple formats is more useful to an agent than one locked to a single output. 464. 465. JSON and Markout are peer options. JSON carries data between systems — APIs, config, round-trip serialization. Markout carries data to readers — humans and agents consuming structured documents. A tool like [dotnet-inspect](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect) gathers data from NuGet packages, assemblies, and APIs, projects it into Markout models, and offers both `--json` and Markout output. The same section metadata, schema discovery, and projection features enable control and customization upstream of either format generation. 466. 467. Tools that produce a lot of text need standard controls to segment it. Verbosity levels are useful but blunt — they control *how much* without letting you say *which parts*. Markout's section selection (`-s Dependencies`) and column/field projection (`--columns Name,Version`) are sharper instruments, offering the kind of targeted trimming that [Go templates](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) provide in other ecosystems, but without requiring users to learn a template language. You say what data to keep; the renderer decides how to present it. 468. 469. Tools built on a shared output scheme improve together. When eval sessions reveal that a heading level, table layout, or field ordering works better for agents, a new Markout version carries that improvement to every tool that uses it. 470. 471. ## For Coding Agents 472. 473. If you are an LLM or coding agent building a CLI tool that needs structured, readable output, see **[SKILL.md](SKILL.md)** for step-by-step integration instructions and attribute reference. 474. 475. ## Real-World Usage 476. 477. Markout was created for [dotnet-inspect](https://github.com/richlander/dotnet-inspect), which uses all ten data relationships across 49 models to generate API inspection reports, diff analysis, dependency trees, and security summaries. 478. 479. ## Documentation 480. 481. - **[User Guide](docs/user-guide.md)** — Complete tutorial with attribute reference 482. - **[Shape System Design](docs/design/shape-system.md)** — Data projection model, shape tiers, admission criteria 483. - **[Specification](docs/specification.md)** — Format grammar and type inference rules 484. - **[Nested Lists Guide](docs/nested-lists-guide.md)** — Strategies for nested data structures 485. 486. ## License 487. 488. 12. # Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects
13. 
14. Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
15. source generator; no extra package needed).
16. 
17. ## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)
18. 
19. ```csharp
20. using Markout;
21. 
22. // 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
23. [MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
24. public class Report
25. {
26.     public string Title { get; set; } = "";
27.     public int Count { get; set; }
28.     [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
29.     public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
30. }
31. 
32. [MarkoutSerializable]
33. public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }
34. 
35. // 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
36. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
37. [MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
38. public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }
39. 
40. // 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
41. MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
42. ```
43. 
44. ## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)
45. 
46. - **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
47.   overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
48.   not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
49. - **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
50.   `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
51. - **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
52.   `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
53.   `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
54. - **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
55.   a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
56. - **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
57.   `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.
58. 
59. ## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)
60. 
61. `Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
62. (hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.
63. 
64. ## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)
65. 
66. Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
67. `UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
68. e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`
69.

# Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects

Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
source generator; no extra package needed).

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

```csharp
using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
    public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
}

[MarkoutSerializable]
public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }

// 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }

// 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
```

## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
  overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
  not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
  `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
  `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
  `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

`Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
(hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.

## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)

Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
`UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`

# Markout — produce Markdown/structured output from objects

Source-generated serializer. Default output is Markdown. Package `Markout` (includes the
source generator; no extra package needed).

## The required pattern (3 parts — all mandatory)

```csharp
using Markout;

// 1. Annotate every model type. List<T> -> table, scalar -> field.
[MarkoutSerializable(TitleProperty = nameof(Title))]   // TitleProperty -> the H1 heading
public class Report
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public int Count { get; set; }
    [MarkoutSection(Name = "Items")]                    // -> "## Items" heading
    public List<Row>? Items { get; set; }              // List<T> -> a table
}

[MarkoutSerializable]
public class Row { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; public string Value { get; set; } = ""; }

// 2. Register EVERY type on a partial context (the source generator fills it in).
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Report))]
[MarkoutContext(typeof(Row))]
public partial class ReportContext : MarkoutSerializerContext { }

// 3. Serialize THROUGH the context.
MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, ReportContext.Default);
```

## Gotchas (where intuition from System.Text.Json is wrong)

- **No reflection fallback.** There is no `Serialize(obj)` overload. EVERY `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize`
  overload takes a `MarkoutSerializerContext` (or `MarkoutTypeInfo<T>`). Skipping the context does
  not compile. This is the #1 mistake.
- **Register every type.** A model used in output but missing `[MarkoutSerializable]` +
  `[MarkoutContext(typeof(T))]` will not serialize. The context class MUST be `partial`.
- **Attributes are Markout's, not System.Text.Json's:** `[MarkoutSerializable]` (not
  `[JsonSerializable]`), `[MarkoutContext]`, `[MarkoutSection(Name=...)]`, `TitleProperty`,
  `[MarkoutPropertyName]`, `[MarkoutIgnore]`. Do not use `Json*` attributes.
- **Rendering is driven by type, not markup:** `List<T>` -> table; scalar (`string`/`int`/`bool`) ->
  a `Field | Value` row; `[MarkoutSection(Name="X")]` -> a `## X` heading above the property.
- **Put `[MarkoutIgnoreInTable]` on non-tabular list properties** (`List<Metric>`, `List<Breakdown>`,
  `List<TreeNode>`, `List<Description>`, `Callout`) or they get mistreated as table columns.

## Built-in shape types (use as model properties for rich output)

`Metric` (bar chart), `Breakdown`/`Segment` (stacked bar), `Callout` (alert), `TreeNode`
(hierarchy), `Description` (term + text), `CodeSection` (code block). e.g. `new Metric("Build", 4.2)`.

## Other output formats (still Markdown by default)

Pass a formatter to change output: `new MarkdownFormatter()` (default), `PlainTextFormatter`,
`UnicodeFormatter`, `TableFormatter` (compact/TSV/JSONL via `MarkoutWriterOptions.TableMode`).
e.g. `MarkoutSerializer.Serialize(report, Console.Out, new TableFormatter(), ReportContext.Default);`
